items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: I said, "Mr. Johnson, this is a school."

ctx.x: I was teaching Clifford Brown in '45 and '46 and going into '47. Then I got sick of it. I got sick of it down there because when you're teaching in those schools, nowadays, you have 40 in a class. But only 5 of them want music. The rest of them want recreation. And they come in the class and socialize and throw rubbers and bottles at you, anything, and have a good time. And so, I wasn't in for that. That was for some young kid that didn't know any different. I've been all around the world. I'm going to be…

them solfeggion and teaching them how to tell what key they were in. And beginning to get Melodia books and teach them how to read the music, he come in there and he said, "Listen, Mr. Wooding, I think you just should just let them sit here and sing and enjoy themselves." This was a school. I said, "Mr. Johnson, this is a school." Said, "I know, but that's what the orders are that I got from the Board of Education." In other words, he was saying some of them going to be cooks anyhow, waitresses and so, so why…
